Audi Is Training Humanoid Robots to Take Over Certain Factory Operations
6 photos
Photo: Audi
There are already several carmakers actively testing ways to incorporate humanoid robots into their assembly processes. From German BMW to South Korean Hyundai, each of them has gotten in bed with various robotics startups for this task, and they are in various stages of implementing such solutions. Much later than its competitors, German Audi announced this week it is doing the same.
The brand with four rings said during the NVIDIA GTC Berlin event that a project meant to determine the merits and usefulness of humanoid robots in automotive manufacturing is already underway, with assistance from Dassault Systèmes and NVIDIA.
The carmaker chose machines made by German startup Agile Robots for the task at hand, without actually naming the solution it uses. For the record, though, Agile offers at the moment only a single humanoid robot, called ONE, in a number of configurations.
The machine stands 68.5 inches (174 cm) tall, making it ideal for use in places designed around the average human height, like Audi's assembly facilities, and tips the scales at 152 pounds (69 kg).
Equipped with two legs (or a mobile platform, depending on needs) and two arms, the robot uses cameras and LiDAR to get a sense of its surroundings, moving around at about the same speed as an average human. When it needs to lift something, it can easily do so, as long as the thing it lifts doesn't weigh more than 44 pounds (20 kg).
Audi is looking at ways of deploying the Agile robot in parts sequencing at its main Ingolstadt facility. In a nutshell, it would have it pick the right parts, in the right order, and have them delivered to the right workstation.
It doesn't sound all that complicated, but it kind of is, really. Audi itself says that sequencing operations at Ingolstadt require around one million picks every single day. Not only that, but the robots must make sense of parts of various shapes and sizes, packaged or not, and many times mixed together in the same containers.
The robot uses its vision system to see the parts and an undisclosed AI system to determine what it sees. When the correct part is identified, it picks it up with help from its arms, which are equipped with tactile sensors.
Agile's robot performs the task assigned to it both in the virtual world, using an application developed by Dassault Systèmes and the NVIDIA Omniverse libraries, and in the real world. We're not told exactly how far along testing is.
If the trials deliver the expected results, Audi plans to integrate Agile bipedal robots in assembly and production alongside human workers. On a corporate level, that means reduced manual workload and better efficiency. For the human workforce, though, this new level of automation likely means something else entirely.

This New Dash Cam Looks Like a Smartwatch, Surprisingly Cheap
15 photos
Photo: Vueroid
Dash cam maker Vueroid has just come up with a brilliant idea: a dash cam that looks like a smartwatch to introduce new customers to this world of permanent eyewitnesses behind the wheel.
The purpose of the H1 QHD Infinite is to make it as straightforward as possible for first-time dash cam buyers to choose, install, and start using such a device. That’s why it’s fitted with a 1.6-inch circular display that reminds you of the one you typically wear on your wrist, also boasting a user interface supposed to make setting up the dash cam and accessing its files as easy as 1-2-3.
Sure, everything sounds good on paper, but is it really that impressive in real life? While that’s hard to say until I hold this dash cam in my hand, there are several things that you must keep in mind when looking at the H1 as your first dash cam ever.
Photo: Vueroid This is a single-channel dash cam, meaning that it only records what happens in front of your car. A rear camera to also keep an eye on what happens in the back or a secondary camera to monitor the cabin is not available.
The H1 wasn’t supposed to be part of a dual-camera configuration , so it doesn’t come with any extra ports. What you see is what you get, so you install it on your windshield, and that’s pretty much it.
The H1 Infinite’s circular dash cam is probably easy to use, but based on my experience, you really won’t interact much with the screen. If you ask me, it’s more important for a dash cam to have an advanced mobile companion app than a large screen because it’s a lot more convenient and straightforward to access your recordings and set up the device from your mobile device.
Photo: Vueroid Once the dash cam is up there on your windshield, touching the screen and setting up everything isn’t as comfortable as you’d expect it to be, especially if you place it behind the rear-view mirror.
The good news is that the H1 comes with a mobile companion app, so if you feel more comfortable doing everything on your smartphone, this is probably the right approach. The app can connect to your dash cam via the built-in Wi-Fi support, but Vueroid, the company that built this device, says you can also connect to the H1 directly using a USB-C cable. It’s unclear how this works and whether you have to use the power port for this connection, but I’ll get more data on this once I receive a review sample.
I currently access all my recordings on my dash cam from my mobile phone, and this feels much easier primarily because I have a larger screen to preview them before the download. I also don’t need to mess with cables, and considering all my recordings are 1-minute long, the download time typically comes down to just a few seconds.
Photo: Vueroid As for the recording quality, this is something I’ll have to discover during my hands-on time with the dash cam. On paper, it doesn’t look bad at all, as it’s fitted with a Sony Starvis 2 IMX675 sensor that can record videos at 2,560 x 1,440 pixels.
To be honest, I would’ve expected this dash cam to support 60 fps, but it only goes as high as 30 fps, despite being a single-channel camera.
It has built-in GPS, a speaker, and a microphone, as it also supports voice commands for quick things, like opening the Wi-Fi for a connection to your mobile device. The microSD support allows you to expand the storage capacity with up to 512 GB of storage.
One of the things that caught my attention is the advertised support for parking monitoring without a hardwire kit - such a kit is also available separately, but Vueroid says you might not need it because a more convenient option is available. This option is parking monitoring when the dash cam is connected to an external battery, meaning that you’ll have to plug it into a power bank and leave the power bank inside the car while you’re away.
Photo: Vueroid I obviously wouldn’t do that, especially when the vehicle is parked outside, and especially if it's parked in direct sunlight. Getting the hardwire kit is the right way to go for parking monitoring, despite the professional installation that might be required if you’re not familiar with this type of thing.
Otherwise, the H1 Infinite might not necessarily be the best dash cam on the market, but it could give birth to a new product category - dash cams that resemble smartwatches for a more familiar approach. The best thing is the selling price, as Vueroid knows it couldn’t charge a premium for these specifications, so if you want the H1, you only need to pay $149 . This makes it one of the cheapest dash cams on the market, albeit you’ll have to spend $34.99 more on the hardwire kit and more dollars on a microSD card.

The 2027 Toyota Crown Signia Is Now Slightly More Expensive Than Last Year, But Also Better Equipped
7 photos
Photo: Toyota Motor Corporation
The Japanese automaker's division, Toyota Motor North America ( TMNA ), has revealed the pricing and specification details for the 2027 Crown Signia mid-size crossover SUV.
Slowly but steadily, TMNA is updating its full-line pricing list to the 2027 model year, and so far we have been announced of the details regarding the 2027 bZ and bZ Woodland EVs, the ultra-popular Camry mid-size sedan, the returning C-HR (now also an EV), the beloved Corolla series, including the Corolla Cross, the family-oriented Grand Highlander, the Prius hybrid and PHEV, the iconic Land Cruiser, and the Crown flagship sedan.
Now it’s time to also check out the goodies for the 2027 Toyota Crown Signia premium mid-size crossover SUV, which returns to the new model year with “a sophisticated blend of elegant design, premium comfort, and capable performance.” Pricing have gone up slightly, from the 2026 Crown Signia XLE and Limited ($44,690 and $49,090) to $44,890 for the XLE and $51,155 for the Limited grade, respectively sans the DFC.
For the 2027 model year, the major updates include a new “Inked” exterior paint color, while the Advanced Technology Package, previously optional on the Limited grade, will now be offered as part of the standard perks. The latter includes a Panoramic View Monitor, Lane Change Assist, Traffic Jam Assist (Active Drive Connect Trial or Subscription Required, 4G Network), Front Cross-Traffic Alert, Front and Rear Parking Assist with Automatic Braking, as well as outer mirrors with puddle lights and a reverse tilt-down feature.
Meanwhile, Inked replaces the black exterior color for the entire range. Otherwise, the 2027 Crown Signia remains as before: it “features a dynamic profile defined by a long, sweeping roofline, a monochromatic grille, and wide fenders.” There are color-matched elements, optional 21-inch wheels, available two-tone exterior paints, mixing Storm Cloud, Oxygen White, Finish Line Red, or Bronze Age with a black roof, and more.
Inside the cabin, the company features standard leather-trimmed, heated, and ventilated front seats, soft-touch materials, bronze-metallic finishes, a fixed panoramic moonroof on the Limited trim, and a 60/40 second-row fold-flat seat design to create a 6.5-foot-long cargo area with up to 68 cubic feet of storage space.
Under the hood resides the standard Toyota Hybrid Electric Vehicle system with the 2.5-liter DOHC four-cylinder engine paired with a hybrid transaxle and a bipolar Nickel-Metal Hydride battery. It has an estimated 238 combined horsepower and a combined 38 MPG rating. There’s also standard electronic On-Demand All Wheel Drive (AWD) with 100:0 to 20:80 force distribution.
The 2027 Crown Signia mid-size CUV models will arrive at Toyota dealerships before the end of the year, featuring 19- or 21-inch alloy wheels, LED projector low- and high-beam headlights, a 12.3-inch touchscreen with Toyota Audio Multimedia, Qi-compatible vertical wireless charging and five USB-C charge ports for the XLE, as well as a premium JBL audio system with 11 speakers including a subwoofer and amplifier, Digital Key capability, and more.

2027 Subaru Outback Becomes More Affordable Than Last Year in America, Now Starts at $32,995 MSRP
7 photos
Photo: Subaru
The current 2026 Subaru Outback mid-size crossover SUV starts from $34,995, but the new model year brings with it a fresh entry-level model and a new starting point of $32,995 sans the destination and delivery of $1,545. Even better, there are additional price reductions for some of the other trims as well.
Earlier this month, Subaru of America announced its September and year-to-date tallies, with the previous month showing an improvement of 13.2% compared to last year and 52,056 vehicle deliveries. The Forester compact crossover SUV returned at the top of the Subaru roster ahead of the Crosstrek, and even the Crosstrek had a good performance, up almost two percentage points last month.
On the other hand, Subaru still has its work cut out for it during the final quarter to come out of the woods, as total nine-month sales stood at 475,878, which is 1.5% less than last year. The Outback, meanwhile, has even more space to recover because it’s down 10% after nine months compared to last year. As such, it’s a good thing that Subaru is already searching for a solution.
The 2027 Subaru Outback now deliveries enhanced affordability with a new base model titled simply Outback, which kicks off at $32,995, while the previous entry-level model, Premium, remains at $34,995 just like last year. Even better, the Outback Limited is now $39,995, down $1,720 from the 2026 model year; the Touring starts at $43,495 (-$1,900), the Limited XT at $43,595 (-$770), the Touring XT at $46,595 (-$1,400), and the adventurous Wilderness goes from $43,995, which is down $1k from last year.
Even some of the options are now cheaper: the bundle for rain-sensing wipers, Navigation, Heated Steering Wheel, Moonroof, Wireless Charger is now $2,045 (-$225), while the Moonroof, Navigation, and Surround View Monitor pack is $1,995(-$50) now.
“The return of an entry-level Subaru Outback trim for 2027 underscores our commitment to providing consumers with affordable, safe, and reliable vehicles,” said Jeff Walters, President and COO, Subaru of America, Inc. “Now, more than ever, we’re focused on offering vehicles designed to meet the budget and needs of families and new car buyers looking for value and capability.”
The new base 2027 Subaru Outback has a new 12.1-inch Subaru Multimedia System, a 12.3-inch full digital instrument cluster, EyeSight® Driver-Assist Technology, DriverFocus® Distraction Mitigation System, heated front seats, 8.7 inches of ground clearance, and more, all standard perks. Also new for the 2027 model year, the Outback Limited XT brings Subaru’s Highway Hands-Free Driving Assist.
Meanwhile, the 2027 Subaru Outback Wilderness gets the driver-assistance features as part of an options package, and three new colors are available for the range: Sand Dune Pearl, Daybreak Blue Pearl, and Snowfall White Silica, which is all-new.
